Messages.Author: Dean Randall Flemming
Messages.Body:
Dear fellow ghazi ( which is Turkish for ``jyhad fighters创),

I notice several complaints about wallpaper, and since I share them I
wonder if we could not establish some alternate card readings and
rulings. This has been done for the game Shadowfist. There is a set of
alternate card readings called Retrofist. Maybe after jyhad players
have discussed new readings thoroughly and somehow voted on them, then
there could be alternate tournament games using the new readings for
fun.

Even cards which are fairly good but of which players have far too
many, especially with the unconscionable reprints of Sabbat War, even
these cards could have alternate readings. Players would simply deface
their extra Barrens and Elder Libraries with a pen inscribing the new
readings. After all, how many Lucky Blows does a player need? And what
clever, innovative but not powerful card ideas are players
contemplating? I think almost all of would agree that any small group
of players could have come up with a hundred low-powered card ideas
better than the unimaginative twaddle dreamed up for Sabbat War. Not
that there are not several rather good and interesting cards in said
expansion, but after such a long time on the drawing boards, one must
conclude that some people have been paid poorly for not a lot of effort.

Therefore, I hope you all shall start sharing your card ideas, so we
can do something with our junk. I suggest the card ideas should be
commenserate in power to the rarity of the card they are replacing, for
the sake of fairness in the matter of collection. Furthermore, it would
be easier for re-writing the cards and more challenging for the amateur
designers if the new card ideas approximated the present idea of the
card being replaced.

Dean Randall Flemming,
Toronto and Seoul, Korea

Sent via Deja.com
http://www.deja.com/

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <927hr2$jeq$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>, Dean Randall Flemming
<deanfl...@my-deja.com> writes

>Players would simply deface
>their extra Barrens and Elder Libraries with a pen inscribing the new
>readings. After all, how many Lucky Blows does a player need?

None of these cards you mention are wallpaper though.

All three are great cards, in the right deck. What makes them wallpaper
is assuming that:

1) They don't have a place in decks (so you don't play them)
2) Putting them in inappropriate decks.

Immortal Grapple would look like wall-paper in a deck designed to go to
range and throw lids. It's just the wrong deck for it.

Lucky Blow is good for decks that want to do a bit more damage, using
fight-back as defence, or which have problems generating extra damage.
The Barrens is highly, highly useful for card cycling, and card cycling
is a very powerful ability when used well. Elder Library is also highly
useful for decks that need to generate relatively large card combos.
The extra cards on hand let you see what you've got coming up.

--

IMO, the best way to deal with the fact that the ally cards are somewhat
redundant is to introduce new cards to make allies better. Vagabond
Mystic is one such card. New cards for, say, Necromancy could do that
in Final Nights, or generic cards, or whatever.

That way, the cards are made less corner case by making the cases in
which they can be played more common - since more people will *want* to
play them.

Messages.Author: Dean Randall Flemming
Messages.Body:
Dear fellow jyhad players,

I admit that my submission was not a perfected dissertation able to
withstand a withering examination, however I do feel that many of its
points were deliberately misunderstood.

By wallpaper I not include cards which one would never use, but
those of which most players have many more than they could possibly use.
Twenty Lucky Blows one might use, but thirty? Ten barrens, but twenty?

I have since remedied my deficient attention to the websites
devoted to jyhad, and I have noted the particularly good card ideas on
the jyhad on line site. Many of them are low-powered and well-balanced.
So why are people adverse to making an alternate play environment where
these or similar ideas are used?

Looking at the cards on that particular site I find many superior
to the new cards in Sabbat War. I think Sabbat War, for one thing, does
not have many new political cards.

Sincerelely,

Dean Randall Flemming,
Toronto and Seoul

On the other hand many card ideas in some other sites are clearly
fantasies by power-gamers. These I think most would vote to leave where
they belong.

Perhaps because nobody shares your belief that Sabbat War's cards are
somehow "inferior". I doubt most of us are averse to using some of
the card ideas; I've played with people who WERE using some of the
card ideas just to find out what they were like. But simply put, the
original game is sufficiently complex and sufficiently entertaining
that none of us see a need to haul out our Lucky Blows and start
hand-creating a totally different play environment.

Your posts read almost like "viva la revolution!", if you want the
truth. You didn't like the cards in Sabbat War. Congrats on being
one of the few people, if not the ONLY person, who didn't. So now you
want to go off and create your own "sideline" variant with your own
cards, figuring you can somehow do "better" than White Wolf, because
you weren't happy? Cry me a river.

> Looking at the cards on that particular site I find many superior
>to the new cards in Sabbat War. I think Sabbat War, for one thing, does
>not have many new political cards.

That's because the Sabbat are not inherently political. They tend to
beat hell out of each other to solve disputes. The Lasombra are
supposed to be the main political force in the Sabbat, and their
cards/disciplines reflect the Sabbat style as well; Dominate,
Political Struggle, Power Structure... no raw "vote gainers" like
Presence.

Sorry you didn't like Sabbat War. But I think you may just have been
hoping for your own personal expansion; I'd advise being happy that we
got one at ALL.

Messages.Author: wes
Messages.Body:
You know, I kind of like the idea of designing new cards. If done by
consensus and with a genuine attempt to keep the new cards fair, this could
be a lot of fun. I have looked at the custom cards on some sites and there
are some genuinely good ideas although I think some are way too powerful.

The thing that scares me about this exercise is just that White Wolf will
apparently never use any of the cards we invent for copyright purposes. Is
there any way around this? Hell, anything I design can be used WITH my
permission and I'll sign whatever release forms they require! I'd be
thrilled just to see one of my cards actually get printed.

LSJ, would you mind letting us in on the actual policy on this? I assume you
would be involved with the creation of new cards at some level. How is this
done?

In any case, I will open the bidding with the following ideas. Please
analyze them to death if you like until we either lose interest or create
potentially cool cards.

1) I had an idea for a card to help out the Followers of Set. Basically the
idea is to manipulate opposing vampire's votes for the use of the FoS. My
original name for the card was 'Abuse of Power' and it basically involved
adding a bleed modifier based on the number of votes of a vampire of the
FoS' prey. This could alternatively be used as an intercept bonus since
this is something the Setites sorely lack. So the text would read something
like this: 'Reaction: this reacting Setite gains an intercept bonus
equivalent to the number of votes of a ready vampire controlled by the
reacting methuselah's prey'. Thematically, this would represent the Setites
having their hands in every pie and using the influence of others for their
own ends.

2) Ghouls! I know some of the cards already either have the word in their
card text like Ghoul Retainer or most likely ARE meant to be ghouls such as
Tasha Morgan or Mr. Winthrop... but I was thinking it would be interesting
to add a bunch of allies that have a specific set of traits. The main
advantage of any ghoul in the World of Darkness is that they basically
operate during the day. If a ghoul takes an action during the day, it should
be VERY hard for a vampire to block them without getting a bad case of
sunburn. Think about allies that have the equivalent of 'Day Operation' (or
something along those lines) but have limitations such as expensive costs
and lack of inherent bleeding ability maybe. This would be a very powerful
ally that could be used either to get equipment (later to transfer to those
who really need it) or perhaps bleed with another card such as Computer
Hacking. Actions such as Bum's Rush and Arson would become a lot more
powerful with these minions so perhaps limiting the ghouls to taking only
non-directed actions as well. I like the idea but I can see this becoming so
easily broken as to ruin the intention. This would hopefully make allies in
general more useful and all those useless anti-ally cards would become more
common. I know this idea is probably crap but it seems like fun to me.

Ok, start ripping them apart now... ready? Go!

Cheers,
WES

Messages.Author: Dean Randall Flemming
Messages.Body:
Dear fellow Jyhad players,

I am sorry that I did not emphasize sufficiently that I wished for
new card ideas to be balanced in such a way that a new common would be
written for an old common, a new uncommon for an old uncommon, et
cetera. I have seen new card ideas on the many sites out there which are
sufficiently interesting and sufficiently limited so as to be neither
needless nor unbalancing. Especially cards for neglected disciplines or
for entirely new game concepts need not be powerful to be useful or
interesting.

I enjoyed many of the new cards for Sabbat War. The storage cards
are a new idea. However, I did not see the need for some of the new
small vampires with the usual discipline mix. As for reprints! Why not
reprint Vampire: The Eternal Struggle? New players who are interested in
beginning Jyhad could buy the basic set. The pre-built decks could still
be sold with some modification. If I were a new player, why would I
prefer to spend all my money on Sabbat War, which does not have most of
the rares or clans from the first set, when I could instead buy some of
each and spend the same amount of money on a more interesting small or
large collection?

Sincerely,
Dean Randall Flemming
Toronto and Seoul

>The new cards which were designed to improve aspects of the
>metagame - the weapon helpers and weenie hosers - seem inadequate.

Why? The cards are not designed to be hosers but hindrances. If you
can hose a deck with a couple of cards, the cards stand a strong chance
of being unbalanced.

As I've pointed out before, the idea is not to hose another deck, but to
survive long enough to get ousts. You don't need enough defence in a
deck to completely hose all other decks. Mind-sets like that will get
you nowhere.

In article <92h7no$m79$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>,
Dean Randall Flemming <deanfl...@my-deja.com> wrote:
> Dear fellow Jyhad players,
>
Dear Dean,
Thanks for the polite responce. It makes a refreshing change.

Your points are totally valid and in a perfect world would have come to
fruition. The reality is that dollars are a stronger market force than
player utopia.

> I am sorry that I did not emphasize sufficiently that I wished
for
> new card ideas to be balanced in such a way that a new common would be
> written for an old common, a new uncommon for an old uncommon, et
> cetera. I have seen new card ideas on the many sites out there which
are
> sufficiently interesting and sufficiently limited so as to be neither
> needless nor unbalancing. Especially cards for neglected disciplines
> or for entirely new game concepts need not be powerful to be useful or
> interesting.
>

Granted. These cards and more will probably be seen in Final Nights.
However, WW could not have printed Final Nights straight 'off the bat'
as it were. There had to be some kind of base set freely available from
which to build on. That gives two alternatives: V:TES basic, or Sabbat.
There are solid reasons for choosing Sabbat....

> I enjoyed many of the new cards for Sabbat War. The storage cards
> are a new idea. However, I did not see the need for some of the new
> small vampires with the usual discipline mix. As for reprints! Why not
> reprint Vampire: The Eternal Struggle?

There are a few reasons for (re)printing SW over V:TES basic. WW did not
know the depth of the V:TES market when the rights to the game reverted
to them. What they did know was that there was player demand for more
Sabbat cards as both print runs from WotC had sold out some time
previous, whereas Jyhad & V:TES had not. If they (re)printed Sabbat it
would sell to existing players, with the right marketing it would sell
to new players and with the inclusion of some new cards it would sell to
the die-hard player base too.

A reprint of V:TES would not automatically do that. Basic V:TES has been
printed in it's two forms in high volume (compared to Sabbat) and in
some locales the market is saturated with V:TES or more usually Jyhad.
Even with new cards this would result in a slow pick up from
distributors from WW. Distributors probably had Jyhad and V:TES in their
warehouses for a reallllly long time when WotC first printed them. Even
now you can pick up Jyhad packs in bargain bins in some parts of the
world. If a V:TES reprint was totally the right thing to do in ajn ideal
world to get newbies playing, if distributors and shops don't buy it-
there's no point. It's mercenary and business-like, but required in
order for the game to survive in the long term.

A sabbat reprint (that sold out quickly, lets not forget) builds up the
player base and satisfies the older players as far as it can. It also
helps sell through any malingering Jyhad/V:TES packs that shops have
lying around, maybe even creating a little demand in the market place
for the older basic sets and expansions (the stock of which [DS & AH]
WotC turned over to WW, albeit in limited quantities).

Now when WW reprint the basic set in late 2001/2002 (assuming it is
considered viable) the distributors and retailers will be more willing
to place orders for it. BTW if you are thinking 'damn- i havn't seen any
packs of Jyhad/V:TES is a long while round here, what's this limey fool
talking about? You have to consider that this is the case in (some parts
of) Northern America. And that's all that matters. That's where most of
the print run will end up.

Small vampires were really needed too, incidently. The tournament scene
was dominated by Camarilla clans because they had more depth in the
number of vampires to choose from. SW goes some way to redressing the
balance of power. Vampires are usually the best cards from any set,
simply because they increase your minion card options and make
skill-based decks more consistant.

> New players who are interested in beginning Jyhad could buy the basic
> set. The pre-built decks could still be sold with some modification. >
If I were a new player, why would I prefer to spend all my money on >
Sabbat War, which does not have most of the rares or clans from the >
first set, when I could instead buy some of
> each and spend the same amount of money on a more interesting small or
> large collection?
>

They will get that chance and when they do they will be safe in the
knowledge that WW has done it's homework and the likelihood that there
will be further cards to follow is stronger than it would be if SW had
not been printed.

WW seem to have made the correct decisions so far for the long-term fate
of the game. Hopefully sales of Final Nights will be strong enough to
warrant a basic set reprint. They should be. Pre-con decks are the way
forward for new players. SW had them and they were good. FN is set to
have them and if V:TES basic set has them too, then things can only be
good for WW and all concerned. More people are playing now as a result
of the handling of SW by WW. Generally this is a good thing, obviously
the only setback being Andrew Davidson's interest in the game. *shrug*

You take the rough with the smooth.

> Sincerely,
> Dean Randall Flemming
> Toronto and Seoul
>

Dear fellow Jyhad palyers,

I realize that this reply is a little late.



I am not sure I understand this explanation. If there are indeed so
many boxes of Jyhad and Vampire:The Eternal Struggle out there on the
shelves and in the warehouses, then why would there be any need to
reprint cards from them? Granted that the publishing company makes no
new profits from these old cards, but I think that more sales of Sabbat
War could have been generated from old players who would have been
happy to buy more boosters or boxes. Presumably distributors and
retailers would be much happier to get rid of all the old stuff.

This is all moot, since the publication has taken place.

Which returns me to my original proposal that Jyhad players formally
adopt new cards for play. Other gaming communities do this quite
readily: miniaturists, roleplayers and wargamers not infrequently adopt
house rules which become formalized for convention and tournament play.

or

I am not suggesting Sabbat War should not have been printed! Merely
that it should have been a smaller collection: all the new cards, some
more low-powered new cards and minus all the reprints of crappy cards.
A more judicious selection, in other words.
But again, I am saying that we do not have to rely on White Wolf
for all our fun.

Sincerely,
Dean Randall Flemming

matching cardback... part of the reason why Jyhad is available for
such low prices, not to mention that Jyhad was overprinted first time
'round.

V:TES is out there, but not lots of it, and from what I can tell it's
starting to dry up; it's getting more expensive as it goes.

NEITHER of them are on store shelves, however.

>shelves and in the warehouses, then why would there be any need to
>reprint cards from them? Granted that the publishing company makes no

Because dealers/retailers will not buy and stock "old" product,
correctly realizing that it will not sell. They will, however, stock
"new" product that happens to contain some reprints; as was the case
with Sabbat War, which SOLD OUT promptly.

>new profits from these old cards, but I think that more sales of Sabbat
>War could have been generated from old players who would have been
>happy to buy more boosters or boxes. Presumably distributors and
>retailers would be much happier to get rid of all the old stuff.

Sabbat War sold out almost IMMEDIATELY. Please explain how to
generate more than 100% sales?

As far as "presumably", you presume incorrectly. Distributors *are*
happy to get rid of the old stuff, which is why you can buy from
Potomac, etc. at bargain prices.

Retailers have long since gotten rid of their old stuff, however, and
that does our game NO good at all to have it not on store shelves and
easily available to the average gamer. We NEED new players to
survive; to get those, we HAVE to have product easily available!
Sabbat War attracted new players, and it revitalized interest for old
players. Hence retailers stocked it (briefly, and then stock ran out
due to a sellout).

Retailers are not, however, about to re-stock old stuff that they had
trouble getting rid of in the first place. Don't expect to see boxes
of Jyhad on your store shelves anytime soon.

> This is all moot, since the publication has taken place.

Good thing, too, since the assumptions you make in your message are
butt-fucking wrong, to put it as politely as i can.

> Which returns me to my original proposal that Jyhad players formally
>adopt new cards for play. Other gaming communities do this quite

There is no relation whatsoever between your original proposal and
what you just babbled about above; why not just say "Hey, everyone
ignored me the first time, let me shout this out again in hopes that
someone is listening."

>readily: miniaturists, roleplayers and wargamers not infrequently adopt
>house rules which become formalized for convention and tournament play.

"If Sally jumped off a cliff, would you do it too?"

We did, in fact, adopt "house rules" once; the Golden Tenets, to be
specific. Those are now part of the VEKN tournament rules. Those
rules were also VERY necessary. Your suggestions fall far, far, far,
FAR short of necessary.

Look, Bosco. Just because you were all pissy about Sabbat War not
being everything you expected is not a good reason for everyone to go
drawing on their old cards. As you can see from a different thread,
Sabbat War wasn't 100% perfect for everyone ELSE, either, but we're
all DELIGHTED to have a product that retailers will actually stock.

Please take your idea, which was shitcanned the FIRST time you brought
it up, and deposit it in the proper receptacle ("the circular file"),
where it belongs. Give a hoot--don't pollute!

(70s flashback moment. sorry.)

> I am not suggesting Sabbat War should not have been printed! Merely
>that it should have been a smaller collection: all the new cards, some
>more low-powered new cards and minus all the reprints of crappy cards.
>A more judicious selection, in other words.

Sure, some cards probably shouldn't have been reprinted (Twisting the
Knife? man...), but there were plenty that SHOULD have been. Why are
you worried about "low-powered"? What exactly was so wrong with the
new cards in Sabbat War? SPECIFICALLY, by the way, not vague bullshit
about "oh, they were overpowered" or the like.

> But again, I am saying that we do not have to rely on White Wolf
>for all our fun.

And I am saying... well, I can't post what I'm *really* saying since
it'll get me labelled a thug and a flamer and all kinds of other nice
things that I probably deserve. Suffice it to say that it was two
words and seven letters. Further hints available for $5.00 each.

What I'm saying AFTER the radio edit is that you should perhaps quit
bitching because things didn't go the way you wanted, DEAL with it,
move on with your life, and play the game instead of organizing, well,
a jihad to draw on our old cards. You might find that it's actually
fun anyway; all the rest of us sure seem to.

Damnans doesn't create his cards because he thinks WW sucks; he does
it, as far as I can tell, just because he feels like creating new
cards. More power to him. If a group somewhere wants to use his
cards, that's great. But he doesn't run around saying his should be
the only way.

-- Derek

Actually, this is technically untrue.

JYHAD card backs... well, we know how they are different.

V:TES card backs began the "V:TES" naming convention.

DARK SOVEREIGNS was the same as V:TES.

ANCIENT HEARTS had the (R) symbol instead of the TM after the
"Deckmaster"

SABBAT & SABBAT WAR are the same as V:TES.

I have also encountered "light" and "dark" printed versions of Jyhad,
V:TES, Dark Sovereigns, and Ancient Hearts cards.

I'm sure there are other variants people could talk about
